🇲🇽🎶 <u>"MÉXICO CANTA": SHEINBAUM PRESENTS 7 MEXICAN-AMERICAN SEMIFINALISTS SINGING FOR PEACE</u>

President Sheinbaum presented the seven Mexican-American semifinalists of México Canta 2026, the binational contest where young people sing for peace and against addictions on both sides of the border.

"We talk little about the bond of love, of culture, of everyday life of the families who live on one side and the other of the border — and that bond never breaks," she said. "They are Americans, but they keep feeling Mexican. And that is something truly beautiful."

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>SENATE RECEIVES SHEINBAUM'S FEMINICIDE LAW: UP TO 70 YEARS IN PRISON</u>

Mexico's Senate officially received the presidential initiative for a General Law to Prevent, Investigate, Punish and Repair the Crime of Feminicide — the first nationwide legal framework against the most extreme form of violence against women.

The proposal contemplates sentences of up to 70 years in prison and creates a National Registry of Children and Adolescents Orphaned by Feminicide, to guarantee protection and reparations for indirect victims. Senate president Laura Itzel Castillo said it goes straight to the Justice and Gender Equality commissions — the goal: unified investigation criteria across the country, and an end to impunity.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>MORENA TO DOUBLE-FILTER ITS 2027 CANDIDATES — WITH HELP FROM THE SECURITY CABINET</u>

After controversies over public officials linked to organized-crime networks, Morena announced that every candidate for 2027 will pass two screenings: an internal review by its National Elections Commission, then a second filter with support from Mexico's security cabinet and the INE — checking for criminal ties, violence against women and gender-based political violence.

"We are going to ask the security cabinet to support the review — it is contemplated in the law for parties, but we are requesting it ahead of schedule," said party leader Ariadna Montiel. The process also includes open-source vetting through media and social networks.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>UNAM'S FIRST ONLINE ADMISSION EXAM DIDN'T WEIGH AI: SHEINBAUM</u>

Mexico's UNAM ran its first fully online entrance exam and the results set off alarms: a statistical analysis found applicants scoring above 100 of 120 jumped from the usual 8-9% to almost 30%, with perfect scores even in high-demand programs like Medicine.

President Sheinbaum called it an anomaly of technology, not of university authorities: the exam "did not measure the development of artificial intelligence." She urged aspirants not to cheat — and said it is up to the autonomous university to define the solution.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>SPAIN'S LEFT RALLIES BEHIND SHEINBAUM: "A BEACON OF LIGHT" AGAINST THE FAR RIGHT</u>

In Madrid, lawmakers from PSOE, Sumar and Izquierda Unida held a solidarity act for Mexico and President Sheinbaum, denouncing a "Monroe Doctrine of the 21st century" — the intervention in Venezuela, the siege on Cuba, tariffs on Brazil, meddling in Peru and Colombia.

PSOE deputy Luisa García: Sheinbaum's mandate "is backed by more than 32 million votes of Mexicans who support her fight against poverty and exclusion."

And Izquierda Unida's Enrique Santiago: Mexico's president is resisting US economic pressure and even threats of military intervention "with an intelligence far above normal — and much higher than Mr. Trump's."

REUTERS: Mexican economy falters in May as construction dips
July 23, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Reuters: Mexico's economy "falters" — one negative month in the IGAE index. April posted the sharpest increase in five years; June's preliminary estimate grew 1.7% y/y. Neither of those got a "soars" headline.

The wire reprint is paywalled, so the framing is the story: a volatile monthly series becomes a narrative only on the down months.

CBS/AFP: Mexico mayor killed in town hall months after surviving assassination attempt
July 22, 2026 | 🟢

📰 CBS/AFP on the killing of Temoac mayor Valentín Lavín — and, unusually for this genre, the wire includes the counter-number: homicides in Mexico down nearly half since September 2024.

Fourteen mayors killed since the current government took office in October 2024 — and the same article carries Sheinbaum's security data instead of dropping it.

• "Almost 100 mayors have been murdered in Mexico since 2006"
• "homicides in Mexico have fallen by nearly half since September 2024"

LATIN TIMES: Mexican Journalist Killed in Oaxaca as Violence Against the Press Deepens
July 23, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Latin Times covers the killing of Oaxaca columnist Alejandro Leyva — shot at a roadside food stand after a year of reported threats — naming his beat: state politics, corruption, organized crime. Sixth journalist murdered in Mexico in 2026.

The piece runs the facts straight: his criticism of the state government, the threats he had reported, the impunity record. No editorializing.

• "fourth journalist slain in Mexico since June"
• "no act of violence against journalists should be tolerated"

CBS NEWS: Salazar responds to Sheinbaum's claim that he lied about "El Mayo" capture: "Truth is the truth"
July 22, 2026 | 🟡

📰 CBS gives ex-ambassador Ken Salazar a book-tour slot to repeat his version of the 2024 El Mayo capture. Mexico's FGR calls his claim that the US played no role "false" — the pilot who flew Zambada out has testified to the operation.

The segment is a platform for his new book "Borderlands"; Mexico's own investigation into the US role in the capture appears only as Sheinbaum's accusation.

• "Truth is the truth"

DALLAS MORNING NEWS: Mexican president sends the wrong signal
July 21, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Dallas Morning News editorial board orders Mexico's president to hand over indicted Morena officials to the US — "This is an opportunity," they call it. Same editorial admits Trump pardoned Honduras' convicted drug-trafficker president and cooperates with an indicted Venezuelan official.

The Rocha case rests on El Mayo Zambada's cooperation — the same 2024 capture Mexico is investigating as a US sovereignty violation. Extraditing sitting Mexican officials would be unprecedented; the board treats it as an errand.

• "Refusal to pursue extradition of official will be damaging"
• "Sheinbaum should not test how far those political whims may go"
• "U.S. prosecutors should continue to build this case, wherever it may lead"
